A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GACD research work. Their main texts, appendices, equations, tables and figures are readable and support reliable comparison after matching relocated material.

before.justification: v3 reports original GACD benchmark evaluations, component and hyperparameter ablations, and qualitative analyses in the main text and supplement.

after.justification: v4 retains original empirical evaluations and adds comparison results, amplification-clipping measurements and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: The gradient-based influence estimates, top-1 noun-linked visual grouping, contrastive decoding, amplification constraints and early-stopping rule are retained. The added derivation and grouping explanation document the existing procedure rather than establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: The same captioning and VQA coverage is retained, including AMBER, MSCOCO, LLaVA-QA90, MMBench, MM-Vet, ScienceQA, VizWiz, MME and POPE over MSCOCO, A-OKVQA and GQA. The occlusion example already appears in v3.

E2.justification: Main Table 3 adds M3ID, AVISC and RLAIF-V to the LLaVA-QA90 comparison across the same three backbones, alongside the retained baseline and VCD. These methods already participate in other comparisons; the expansion is confined to this experiment.

E3.justification: v4 adds clipping-rate measurement on POPE and MSCOCO in supplementary Table 12 and runtime as an additional metric in the LLaVA-v1.5 cost comparison, supplementary Table 17. Existing splits, sampling settings, output limits, thresholds and hyperparameter search grids are retained.

E4.justification: The new clipping-rate analysis tests how often the maximum amplification bound becomes active, and the cost analysis gains timing evidence. The existing top-2 grouping ablation has revised results; other component, sensitivity and qualitative analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The mean-and-standard-deviation visual-influence display in Figure 3a and the uncertainty entries for non-greedy sampling in supplementary Table 8 are retained. Neither version adds different run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: Table 3 adds comparator scores while retaining GACD's scores. LLaVA-v1.5's POPE adversarial baseline accuracy changes from 79.4 to 80.9, and supplementary Table 7 revises its random/popular baseline and GACD scores. Supplementary Table 11 changes top-2 results, including InstructBLIP accuracy/F1 from 79.6/80.6 to 82.9/82.5, making the top-1 advantage mixed. New entries report clipping rates of 0.04%/0.07% and baseline/VCD/GACD runtimes of 191/383/385 ms.

T1.justification: New supplementary Section 3 derives the existing amplification-weight formula by equating adjusted visual and prompt influence, yielding Equation 18 and noting the analogous output-dominant case. v3 states the formula without this derivation. The existing Taylor and KL-divergence derivations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about gradient-based self-reflection, mitigation of text-visual and co-occurrence biases, and inference without fine-tuning or auxiliary models. The headline quantitative improvement claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: v4 newly characterizes the maximum amplification cap as a rarely activated precaution. It replaces the top-2 discussion's assertion of diffuse attribution with a tentative explanation involving dilution of a dominant visual token and benefits for only some objects. The white-box requirement and existing applicability limitations are retained.

D1.justification: v4 clarifies CPU-only, interchangeable noun detection and the grouping trigger, adds Qwen architecture entries, and supplies runtime information. PyTorch gradient computation and the spaCy model were already documented in v3. The two new architecture rows share the Qwen2-VL-7B label but specify different LLMs, leaving their mapping ambiguous.

R1.justification: v4 adds Simonyan, Vedaldi and Zisserman's saliency work and cites it when describing gradient-norm importance as an approximation. The introduction reframes auxiliary-model drawbacks from cost to additional error sources and task-specific supervision. The CHAIR reference's publication update is bibliographic rather than a new cited work.

P1.justification: The author-affiliation block and several methodological and explanatory passages are edited. References move after the supplement, while implementation details, computational cost and broader impacts move earlier within it. Most prose and the main narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: v4 adds a clipping-rate table, expands the LLaVA-QA90 and architecture tables, and adds a runtime column to the cost table. Existing figures and tables are repositioned through reflow, and references change from two-column to full-width layout. The substantive figure content is retained.

improvement.justification: The additional LLaVA-QA90 baselines strengthen the comparison, while the amplification derivation, clipping analysis and runtime reporting make the method easier to assess. These are limited gains around an unchanged method and largely retained evidence. Unexplained numerical revisions and the ambiguous duplicated Qwen architecture label limit reproducibility, but the added comparative evidence and technical transparency support a modest net improvement.
